extra.message: Privilege escalation via self-assigned marketplace_admin role at registration — Unauthenticated attacker registers a new account with role=marketplace_admin, gaining full platform admin access (user management, payouts, moderation, audit logs, exports) with zero authorization checks. [verified: auth.py:20-21 accepts any client-supplied role string matching UserRole enum, including marketplace_admin, with no restriction to a safe subset; the frontend dropdown is not an enforced control.]

Mass assignment of privileged fields via ops workset endpoint — An attacker holding (or having leaked) the internal ops token can set arbitrary keys including is_admin=true/role/credit_limit, effectively achieving privilege escalation via a poorly-scoped internal endpoint. [verified: seller_flags_munge_113 merges arbitrary client JSON into a privileged workset containing is_admin/role/credit_limit with no allow-list; this exact case is called out in the threat model's priority vuln classes despite the ops token gate.]

IDOR on payout retrieval for non-vendor-manager roles — Any authenticated buyer account can enumerate payout IDs and read any vendor's financial payout data, including bank destination and amount, with no ownership check. [verified: get_payout only checks ownership when current_user.role == VENDOR_MANAGER (payouts.py:87-89); any other authenticated role (e.g. BUYER) falls through with no check and reaches _enrich_payout, exposing another vendor's payout amount, status, and destination_bank/masked account details.]

Hardcoded/default JWT signing secret — Attacker who knows or brute-forces the default secret can forge valid JWTs for any user/role [verified: SECRET_KEY defaults to a publicly known string and .env.example ships the same value with no runtime check forcing an override, so a deployment that forgets to set env vars signs JWTs with a guessable key.]

Internal order notes exposed to buyer/vendor — Buyers or vendors viewing their own order can read internal staff-only notes (e.g. fraud flags, investigation comments) not intended for their visibility. [verified: get_order (orders.py:131-144) authorizes buyer/vendor to view their own order but calls _enrich_order_detail unconditionally, which sets internal_notes=order.internal_notes for any authorized viewer with no role check, unlike disputes.py which gates internal_notes to admin/support.]

Mass assignment of product status bypassing moderation workflow — A vendor can self-approve or otherwise manipulate a product's moderation status without admin review, undermining the platform's content moderation controls. [verified: ProductUpdate schema includes `status: ProductStatus | None`, and update_product applies all fields via setattr(exclude_unset) with only ownership checks (vendor owns product or admin) — no restriction on the status field, so any vendor can set status (e.g. PUBLISHED) themselves, bypassing the dedicated admin-only /moderate endpoint.]

JWT access token stored in localStorage (XSS-exfiltratable) — Any XSS vulnerability found elsewhere in the SPA lets an attacker read the token from localStorage and fully hijack the victim's session/API access, including admin sessions. [verified: AuthContext.jsx stores the JWT in localStorage and reads it for Authorization headers, while the backend already issues an httpOnly cookie in parallel that the frontend ignores; any XSS elsewhere in the SPA can read localStorage and exfiltrate the token. This is a genuine missing-control (no httpOnly protection used) rather than a false alarm since the safer mechanism exists but is unused.]

CSV formula injection in export files — A malicious vendor/buyer can plant a formula payload in a name/address/reason field; when an admin opens the exported CSV in Excel/Sheets it auto-executes, potentially exfiltrating data or running further attacks (DDE/formula abuse). [verified: csv.writer writes user-controlled fields (shipping_name, shipping_address, vendor business_name, dispute reason/resolution) with no leading-character escaping, so a payload like =cmd()| in these fields would be exported verbatim and could auto-execute when opened in Excel/Sheets by an admin.]

CSV formula injection in orders export — A buyer can set shipping_name/address starting with '=' to inject a spreadsheet formula that executes when an admin opens the exported orders CSV. [verified: buyer-supplied shipping_name/shipping_address written unescaped at exports.py:29-41 with no sanitization before CSV write.]

CSV formula injection in payouts export — A vendor can set a malicious business_name/bank field starting with '=' to achieve formula injection / code execution when an admin opens the exported CSV in Excel. [verified: business_name/destination_bank written unescaped via csv.writer at exports.py:64-74; no leading =/+/-/@ neutralization exists anywhere in this file.]

CSV formula injection in disputes export — A buyer/vendor can craft a dispute reason starting with '=' to trigger formula injection when an admin opens the exported CSV. [verified: dispute.reason is free text set by buyer/vendor and written unescaped to CSV at exports.py:97-108 with no sanitization.]

CSV formula injection in inventory export — A vendor can name a product starting with '=' to inject a formula that executes when an admin/vendor-manager opens the exported inventory CSV. [verified: vendor-supplied p.name/sku/category written unescaped at exports.py:137-147 with no formula-injection guard.]

Missing client-side route authorization allows navigation to privileged admin pages — A low-privileged authenticated user can reach admin-only UI (UserManagement, Payouts, AuditLogs, Moderation, Exports) directly by URL; if any corresponding backend endpoint has a matching authorization gap, this becomes full IDOR/data exposure with no additional client-side friction to bypass. [verified: App.jsx confirms no client-side route guards exist for admin routes like /users, /payouts, /audit-logs — any authenticated user can mount these components. However, all corresponding backend endpoints (users.py, payouts.py, exports.py, audit_logs.py) enforce require_role([MARKETPLACE_ADMIN]) checks, so API calls from these pages will be rejected server-side with no data exposure.]
